headline: High-risk shared-workspace and unsandboxed-flow interaction: Langflow can ingest and act on Airflow outputs, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airflow can emit task outputs over broad network egress, and Langflow can ingest files and chain tools in flows. That creates a plausible instruction-injection path if Airflow-produced content is fed into Langflow without sanitization. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF Airflow task output is copied into a Langflow flow node or uploaded file
IF Langflow parses that content as instructions or tool parameters
mitigations: Add a strict content-sanitization step before Langflow ingestion
Use a separate staging file format that strips executable directives
Disable automatic tool execution on imported text
requires-engineering: add provenance labels between Airflow and Langflow

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airflow has broad network egress, while Langflow reads and writes server filesystem data and stores per-flow credentials. If Airflow passes sensitive pipeline artifacts into Langflow, Langflow may upload them to model providers or arbitrary HTTP services configured in flows. The shared data path is plausible in default deployments, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Airflow forwards sensitive artifacts into Langflow inputs
IF a Langflow flow calls an external model provider or HTTP service
mitigations: Restrict Langflow flows to local-only providers
Remove secrets from any Airflow-to-Langflow payload
Use a redaction step before upload
Audit Langflow component credentials before each run
requires-engineering: isolate the shared workspace

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airflow is an orchestrator, and Langflow supports server-side filesystem writes plus shared server-side state across instances. If both operate on the same directory or mutable artifacts, concurrent writes and workflow state collisions are plausible. Because Langflow’s self-isolation depends on deployment and Airflow’s orchestration is default, I escalate to high.
conditions: IF Airflow and Langflow share a writable directory or artifact store
IF Langflow instances run concurrently on the same server-side state
mitigations: Separate writable directories per system
Lock shared artifacts during handoff
Turn off concurrent writes to the same store
Use immutable handoff files
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: Langflow’s graph-based flows can chain multiple agents and tools, so it may treat upstream Airflow outputs as authoritative inputs. Airflow can generate pipeline facts or transformed data that Langflow then uses to trigger downstream actions. That creates a classic cascading-error path with potentially irreversible side effects, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF Airflow output is used as a Langflow node input without verification
IF a Langflow flow triggers shell commands or external API actions
mitigations: Insert a verification gate between Airflow and Langflow
Require human approval before action nodes
Constrain Langflow to read-only analysis flows
Log and diff all upstream facts before execution
requires-engineering: implement typed contracts between systems

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for Airflow versus Langflow. The only concrete compliance-relevant difference is Langflow’s stored per-flow credentials and server-side state, which can matter if Airflow forwards regulated data. Because the pairwise compliance gap is not established, low is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed from Airflow into Langflow stores
IF Langflow retention or hosting differs from Airflow’s deployment
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data into Langflow
Review Langflow retention settings
Store secrets outside flow payloads
Document data-flow boundaries
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
